title: Crocodiles
objective: After this level you can describe crocodiles and alligators and how to tell them apart.
summary: Crocodilians lurk with eyes, ears and nostrils on top. Crocodiles: V-shaped snout, lower teeth showing. Alligators: U-shaped snout. Tongue salt glands let crocodiles go to sea.

cards.headline: Alligator or crocodile? Wait for it to close its mouth.
cards.body: Alligators, crocodiles, caimans and gharials are all crocodilians, and at a glance they blur together. But a closed mouth gives the game away. So does a trip into seawater.

cards.headline: Built to lurk
cards.body: Every crocodilian is shaped for ambush. Its eyes, ears and nostrils sit on top of its head, so they stay above the surface while the rest of the body hides underwater. It can watch, listen and breathe without showing much more than a bump. From the bank, a waiting crocodile looks like a log with eyebrows.

items.label: Alligator
points: Lower teeth fit inside the upper ones
Big fourth lower tooth hidden in a socket

items.label: Crocodile
points: Some lower teeth show with the mouth closed
That fourth tooth sticks out: a toothy grin

cards.fact: A crocodile's tongue works as a salt pump.
cards.context: Alligators live mostly in fresh water and can handle salt water only briefly, because they have no salt glands. Crocodiles have salt glands in their tongues that get rid of the extra salt. That's how the saltwater crocodile, the largest living crocodilian at up to 23 feet (about 7 meters), can turn up far out at sea.

cards.headline: Crocodilians: explained
learned: Eyes, ears and nostrils on top of the head for ambush
Alligator: U-shaped snout, lower teeth hidden
Crocodile: V-shaped snout, lower teeth showing
Crocodiles' tongue salt glands let them go to sea

questions.prompt: Which one shows some lower teeth when its mouth is closed?

options.label: The alligator
options.rationale: An alligator's lower teeth fit inside the upper jaw.

options.label: Both, equally
options.rationale: This is exactly the difference between them.

questions.explanation: Crocodiles show some lower teeth with the mouth shut; an alligator's lower teeth, including the big fourth one, are hidden.

questions.prompt: Why do alligators stay mostly in fresh water while some crocodiles swim far out to sea?

options.label: Alligators are too heavy to swim in waves
options.rationale: Alligators swim well; salt is their problem.

options.label: Crocodiles drink only rainwater at sea
options.rationale: The difference is getting rid of salt, not what they drink.

options.label: Alligators need much warmer water to hunt
options.rationale: Salt, not temperature, keeps alligators in fresh water.

options.label: Only crocodiles have tongue salt glands

questions.explanation: Tongue salt glands let crocodiles get rid of extra salt; alligators lack salt glands and tolerate salt water only briefly.

questions.prompt: Level 31 named four groups of living reptiles. Which group do caimans and gharials belong to?

options.label: Turtles
options.rationale: Turtles carry shells built from their ribs.

options.label: Lizards and snakes
options.rationale: Caimans and gharials are close kin of alligators and crocodiles.

options.label: The tuatara
options.rationale: The tuatara is its own small group.

questions.explanation: Alligators, crocodiles, caimans and gharials together form the crocodilians, one of the four living reptile groups.
